findings.text: follow-on: the negative control's header names `revision=e7464580` (the base), but the three test ids it ran were introduced by de6f6529d and are absent at e7464580, so the header names the mutated source's revision rather than the tree the run resolved (base source + new tests). The log is bound to the behaviour it records only through the manifest's word; recording the revision of the test tree alongside the mutated source would make the arm self-binding.

follow-on: the --min-score help text changed from '(default: 0.5)' to '(default: Jev ingest gate)', so --help no longer shows the numeric default (0.16) a user would apply; naming the gate is right but the value is no longer readable from help. Stating the value and the gate (for example by the constant's name or its figure) would keep the help actionable, though the done-when did require the gate to be named rather than the literal.

follow-on: the worktree gate logs (gate.log, gate-final.log) carry a revision/tree/command header but record no module.__file__ or a resolved working directory, so they are bound to 506a447 only through the manifest's PYTHONPATH header; naming the imported module path and the resolved cwd on the header lines would make the arm self-binding, the same gap the accompanying fold reviews recorded.

item_verdicts.call_sites: WikiStageOptions and the wiki click default are the two default sites for the wiki ingest threshold; both route through the same constant. The engine call site wiki.py:1063 passes options.min_score through unchanged, so the constant reaches run_parallel_wiki_discovery.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base e7464580. de6f6529d changes wiki.py (7 insertions, 3 deletions: the import, the two defaults, and the help text) and adds 31 test lines. 506a44750 changes only the test file (4 insertions, 3 deletions), normalizing the help assertion to `' '.join(result.output.split())` so it reads the wrapped help output rather than a literal layout. Both commits are conventional and carry bodies; the retry is honest (gate.log shows the fix commit failing on the help test before 506a447 repaired the assertion).
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when is five checks in tests/cli/test_discover_wiki_stage.py plus both test files passing. tests/cli/test_discover_wiki_stage.py proves each: WikiStageOptions().min_score == CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD (test_default_min_score_uses_ingest_gate), a plain discover wiki invocation passes CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD to the engine (test_cli_default_min_score_reaches_engine, asserting on the recorded engine kwargs), an explicit --min-score 0.3 still overrides (test_cli_explicit_min_score_overrides_ingest_gate), and the --min-score help names 'Jev ingest gate' and no longer 'default: 0.5' (test_min_score_help_names_ingest_gate). No literal 0.5 ingest default remains in wiki.py: `git show 506a447:imas_codex/cli/discover/wiki.py | grep -n '0\.5'` returns nothing (rc=1). The named gate passes: 62 passed, EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is exact and single: make the wiki stage's min_score default in imas_codex/cli/discover/wiki.py read CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD from imas_codex/discovery/wiki/graph_ops.py instead of the literal 0.5. The landed change does exactly this at both default sites — WikiStageOptions.min_score (wiki.py:58) and the --min-score click option (wiki.py:1261) both read CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD, imported at wiki.py:22 — and graph_ops.py:29 defines CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD = 0.16, the Jev-calibrated ingest gate.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it is well formed. It records commits de6f6529d and 506a44750, the two changed paths, the gate command with 62 passed EXIT=0 (gate-final.log), a declared negative control at negative-control.log (3 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1), the retry failure (gate.log at de6f6529d: test_min_score_help_names_ingest_gate), a landing line, and both suite arms as baseline_suite and after_suite JSON with their log paths.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed manifest declares changed_paths imas_codex/cli/discover/wiki.py and tests/cli/test_discover_wiki_stage.py; `git diff --stat e7464580..506a447` touches exactly those two files and no path outside them changed. The fragment and figure paths in the node's grant were correctly left unused, since the done-when names no artifact and the node is small (≈ 35 changed lines).

justifications.durability: the tests assert at the seam that carries the value — the kwargs the engine (run_parallel_wiki_discovery) receives for the CLI path, and WikiStageOptions().min_score for the dataclass — rather than on rendering detail, so they pin the behaviour and not the layout. The negative control genuinely reddens three of the four new assertions, so the guard is shown to fire. The retry is recorded and consistent: gate.log at de6f6529d failed only test_min_score_help_names_ingest_gate (1 failed, 61 passed), and 506a447 repaired the assertion rather than the product. The worktree is clean at 506a447. The minor durability gap is that the help assertion couples to the exact phrase 'Jev ingest gate', which the done-when mandated, so a future edit of that phrase re-reddens the test — an acceptable coupling for a user-facing requirement.
justifications.evidence: the reviewed run's own logs are strong on the substance: gate-final.log is a complete after arm at 506a447 reading 62 passed EXIT=0, and negative-control.log is a complete arm reading EXIT=1 with three failing test ids whose assertion bodies are genuine (test_default_min_score_uses_ingest_gate: `assert 0.5 == 0.16`; test_min_score_help_names_ingest_gate: `'Jev ingest gate' in output` False), so the guard is shown to fail when the fix is reverted. I reproduced the head arm independently (62 passed). Two weaknesses keep this out of the top band. First, the negative-control.log header reads `revision=e7464580` — the base — but the three tests it ran were introduced by de6f6529d, absent at e7464580 (`git show e7464580:tests/cli/test_discover_wiki_stage.py | grep -c test_default_min_score_uses_ingest_gate` = 0), so the header names the mutated source's revision, not the tree the run resolved; the log is a base-source + new-tests combination no single commit names and is bound only through the manifest's word. Second, neither the worktree gate logs nor the negative control record module.__file__ or a resolved cwd, so they are tied to 506a447 through the manifest's PYTHONPATH header alone.
justifications.fit: the change follows the repo's idiom and its 'one source of truth' rule directly: it imports the existing CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD and uses it as the default rather than introducing a new literal, and no plan name or section number appears in source or comments. Neither commit message nor source names a plan label. The one fit consideration is that --min-score --help no longer states the numeric default: the old text said '(default: 0.5)' and the new text says '(default: Jev ingest gate)', so a user reading help cannot see the value (0.16) that is actually applied, though the done-when explicitly required the gate to be named instead of 0.5.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the exact goal is met with no deviation: wiki.py imports CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD from graph_ops.py (wiki.py:22), sets the dataclass default (wiki.py:58) and the click option default (wiki.py:1261) to it, and the help text is changed from '(default: 0.5)' to '(default: Jev ingest gate)' (wiki.py:1262). Every done-when bullet is measured by a test and the named gate passes 62 EXIT=0, which I reproduced independently in the reviewed worktree at 506a447 (62 passed, 1 warning in 13.58s, EXIT=0). No literal 0.5 remains in wiki.py.
justifications.reuse: the change reuses the single existing threshold constant instead of duplicating a literal, which is precisely the reuse the repo asks for; it forks no helper and changes no engine behaviour. The two default sites now derive from one value, removing the divergence (0.5 in the CLI versus 0.16 in the engine) that motivated the node.
justifications.scope_discipline: `git diff --stat e7464580..506a447506d3e73a87f51defa4e9bdcf3733bba8` changes exactly two paths — imas_codex/cli/discover/wiki.py (7 insertions, 3 deletions) and tests/cli/test_discover_wiki_stage.py (35 insertions, 3 deletions) — both inside the reviewed manifest's declared changed_paths and the node's exclusive write grant. No other path changed; the graph_ops constant was read, not edited, which is correct since it is not in this node's scope.
